title: Nintendo Reveals Mineru Construct Amiibo Ahead of Ocarina of Time Remake
text:
Nintendo announced the Mineru Construct amiibo will launch on September 17, offering a rare articulated figure that unlocks in‑game rewards across Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom, and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. The news also confirms an upcoming Ocarina of Time remake for the next‑gen Switch.
An official statement from Nintendo today promised that the next mainline entry in the Legend of Zelda franchise is arriving sooner than fans had expected.
According to the release notes shared during the company's developer conference, a brand‑new amiibo figure - the Mineru Construct - will hit the shelves on September 17. Mineru, who appears in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom as an elder sister of King Rauru and a former Sage of Spirit, transforms into a highly articulated action figure that not only poses in real life but also unlocks in‑game rewards when scanned across multiple titles in the series.
The announcement was announced alongside confirmation of an upcoming Ocarina of Time remake that will launch later this year on the next generation of Switch hardware. Unlike most traditional amiibo that feature only a top‑down view of their characters, the Mineru Construct is a walk‑around prop with joints that players can move and pose in the real world.
When scanned into The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, Tears of the Kingdom or Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment, the figure grants a small chance to receive a random in‑game item such as a new piece of armour, a special fabric for Link's paraglider or even a small set of experience‑boosting ingredients that occasionally help players finish quests faster. While the rewards that appear in Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom tend to be low‑tier, the construct's compatibility with Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment is far more rewarding because that title rewards a complete new sword‑play style, full visualisation of Mineru's architectural umbrellas and exclusive combat tutorials that explore the wider Zonai culture.
Players who stream the figure in the physical space can also capture a sense of immersion that connects the game's past and present storylines. Mineru's appearance as a playable character in Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment will allow players to engage with her backstory while witnessing the formative years of the Zonai society that The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom only hinted at.
For collectors who do not regard amiibo as a lease of extra content, the need to own this construct may not be compelling, however the fact that the figure can directly influence the narrative arcs of the franchise grants it a unique status. Nintendo's decision to announce the figure months ahead of time builds anticipation for the game's eventual release and positions the looming Ocarina of Time remake as a future cultural milestone in the series.
Fans who are watching newer releases in the line, year after year, can now look forward to a period where the core Mythos of Hyrule expands once again after the aftermath of the recent 2D and 3D entries
